subject: Interpretation of regression coefficients when computing a CFA with categorical variables

messages.author: 502357d7fd8f8e36
messages.subject: Interpretation of regression coefficients when computing a CFA with categorical variables
parts:
Deal all,

i'd like to compute a CFA over a set of nine indicators which correspond to results in nine ability tests. 6 of these indicators are metric with a small number of categories (5 or less), so I'd like to treat them as categocial. 3 of them are continuous.

I computed a two-factor model CFA using the WLSMV, I specified the ordered variables as well and went for pairwise deletion of missing values.

model2<- 'OB =~sc.unit.lr+sc.unit.umgeklappt+sc.unit.wurfelschlangen+sc.unit.papierfalten
EGO =~ sc.unit.leuchtturm+sc.unit.claudia+sc.unit.verschachtelt+sc.pg.ben+sc.unit.wiese'

fit2<-cfa(model2, data=data.mat, estimator="WLSMV",missing="pairwise", ordered=c("sc.unit.lr", "sc.unit.umgeklappt","sc.unit.wurfelschlangen","sc.pg.ben","sc.unit.leuchtturm", "sc.unit.papierfalten"))
summary(fit2, fit.measures=TRUE, standardized=TRUE, rsquare = TRUE)

I'm able to interpret the fit indices but while comparing lavaan with MPLUS, I got a little bit confused about the output.

How do I have to interpret the STANDARDIZED coefficients? Are they LINEAR regression coefficients or PROBIT regression coefficients? I tried to find some hints in Kline's book. There, it's perfectly explained how to interpret the standardized coefficients for continuous variables, but I can't find a clue for categorical variables.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Interpretation of regression coefficients when computing a CFA with categorical variables
parts: How do I have to interpret the STANDARDIZED coefficients? Are they LINEAR regression coefficients or PROBIT regression coefficients?

It is a probit link, so if you set the argument "std.lv = TRUE" to identify the model by fixing the factor variance instead of a factor loading to 1, then the standardized estimates will be identical to the unstandardized ones.
